title: 16 System Ideas That Keep the Internet From Breaking
subtitle: A beginner map to idempotency, sagas, hashing and more
intro: You tap "pay" once but your phone sends it twice. Should you be charged twice? Good systems say no.
takeaway: System design is how many small services act like one reliable app, even when networks and machines fail.

sections.heading: Everyday analogy: a busy restaurant kitchen
sections.body:
Think of an app like a restaurant. Orders (API calls), chefs (services), storage rooms (databases) and runners (networks) must work together.

Service Discovery is the host who knows which chef is free. Consistent Hashing decides which fridge stores what. Idempotent APIs mean re-sending the same order doesn't cook it twice.

Bloom Filters are a quick "we definitely don't have it" checklist before searching the pantry. JWT Authentication is your stamped wristband to prove you paid.

That kitchen only works if parts can fail safely, which is why these ideas exist.

sections.heading: Why does this exist? To stay up when pieces fail
sections.body:
Distributed Systems split work across many machines so one failure doesn't stop everyone.

- RPC lets one service call another like a function, even far away.
- Saga Design Pattern breaks a big transaction into small steps with undo plans if one step fails.

You need this because phones retry, servers crash, and data grows. It leads to a new risk: complexity itself can break you.

sections.heading: What can go wrong? The fixes become the bugs
sections.body:
More pieces mean more places to fail.

- A bad hash ring sends all traffic to one server.
- Service Discovery with stale info sends you to dead machines.
- A broken saga leaves half an order paid and half not.

Simple beats clever early. Start with clear API Design and add patterns only when you feel real pain.

steps.narration: You send a request; network may duplicate it.
Discovery finds a healthy service instance.
Services talk via RPC to do work.
Saga with JWT ensures steps are authorized and reversible.
Consistent hashing places data; Bloom filter avoids wasted lookups.

quiz.q: What does an Idempotent API guarantee?
options: Same request twice has same effect as once
Data is always on one machine

quiz.q: What can go wrong if usage grows 100x quickly?
options: Consistent hashing and discovery can overload one server or route to dead ones
quiz.why: Hot spots and stale discovery are classic scale failures.

quiz.q: What is the Saga pattern for?
options: Managing a multi-service transaction with compensating steps
quiz.why: Sagas handle distributed transactions without one giant lock.
